summary: Taitsu Kono is a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Hanazono University and under traditional teacher Mumon Yamada, later holding a post at Hanazono University around 2000.

Taixu (1890–1947) worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy, studying under Jichan, Jingan, and Yang Renshan. He served as a monk at Bilu Temple, led the Minnan Buddhist Academy, and founded several Buddhist institutes, academies, and associations.

Taizan Maezumi (1931–1995) worked in Buddhist studies, studying at Komazawa University, Soji-ji, San Francisco State University, and under Baian Hakujun Kuroda, Hakuun Ryōko Yasutani, and Koryu Osaka. He served as a priest at Zenshuji Soto Mission and founded the Kuroda Institute.
Tak Pui Sze is a scholar in sinology and Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at the University of British Columbia under the doctoral supervision of Jinhua Chen.

Taka Yanagisawa (1926–2003) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. She studied at Japan Women's University and served as Director of the Department of Fine Arts at the Tokyo National Research Institute for Cultural Properties.
Takahiko Kameyama works in Buddhist studies and Indology. Attested in 2015, he held posts as a professor at the Institute of Buddhist Studies and as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University.

Takamaro Shigaraki (1926–2014) specialized in Buddhist studies, earning a PhD from Ryukoku University. He served as professor and president (1989–1995) at Ryukoku University, and was chairman and board director of the Society for the Promotion of Buddhism.

Takamatsu Yoshie (1880–1940) studied at Waseda University and the University of Paris. He founded Waseda University and served there as an English teacher, lecturer, professor (from 1915), and Dean of Letters (1930).

Takami Inoue works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. Inoue was a doctoral candidate at the University of California, Santa Barbara (attested 2003) and served as Professor of Shin Buddhist Studies at Otani University.

Takamichi Fukita specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. Fukita studied at Taisho University, Bukkyo University under Yuichi Kajiyama and Shozen Kumoi, and under postdoctoral mentor Heinz Bechert, later lecturing at Bukkyo University (attested 1999).

Takanobu Takahashi is an Indologist and linguist. He studied at the University of Tokyo, Madurai Kamaraj University under Rama. Periakaruppan, and Utrecht University (PhD), later serving at International Buddhist University and the University of Tokyo (1996–2016).

Takanori Kimura is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University. He held positions as a lecturer at Yamaguchi University (attested 1996) and as chief priest at Kaichōji (attested 2003).

Takanori Shintani is a scholar in religious studies, Japanology, and history/archaeology. After studying at Waseda University (~1968–1977), he held posts at the Graduate University for Advanced Studies (~1999–2010) and Kokugakuin University (~2010–2019).

Takanori Unno is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a doctorate at Nagoya University, studying under Yoshifumi Ueda and other scholars. He held posts as an assistant at Nagoya University, lecturer at Aichi Prefectural University, and professor at Meijo University.

Takao Hayashi specializes in Indology and history/archaeology. After earning a PhD at Brown University under David Pingree, he was a researcher at the Harish-Chandra Research Institute and later an assistant professor (1986–1989) and professor (1995–2015) at Doshisha University.
Takao Kagawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Susumu Yamaguchi, Issai Funahashi, and Shoju Inaba, and served as a professor at Bukkyo University.

Takao Maruyama is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tohoku University. He held professorial posts at Rissho University, Shinshu University (where he became professor emeritus), and Mejiro University.

Takao Moriyasu (1948–2024) worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, history and archaeology, and Sinology. He earned degrees from the University of Tokyo and Osaka University, and held professorships at Osaka University (1994–2012) and Kindai University (2012–2015).

Takao Yamagata (1932–2019) was a religious studies scholar who studied at Tohoku University. He held a post at Miyagi Gakuin Women's University (~1969–2003) and served as president of the Japanese Association for the Study of Indian Religions (attested 1997).

Takashi Iwata is an Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University and the University of Hamburg. He served on the faculty at Waseda University as associate professor (~1986–1991) and professor (~1991–2015).
